title: LINQ and async boundaries
summary: Compose a LINQ query, then diagnose an async void handler that cannot be awaited.

scenario.briefing: A dashboard filters positive stock changes and calls a service asynchronously. Keep the query typed and the async boundary observable.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Diagnose a realistic mistake and choose the correct repair.

hints: Materialize with ToList so the return type is a List<int>.

misconceptions.description: Returning a deferred query as a list.
misconceptions.testDescription: The query filters positives and materializes the result.
misconceptions.feedback: A deferred query may read data later. Materialize it with ToList when the method promises a list.

misconceptions.description: Using async void for ordinary methods.
misconceptions.feedback: A try/catch that swallows errors still leaves the caller unable to await completion. Use async Task.

misconceptions.description: Believing LINQ must return the same type as its source.
misconceptions.feedback: LINQ operators can project, filter, group, and reshape into different types.

steps.title: The unobservable handler
steps.prompt: This event handler is async void, so failures cannot be awaited. Select the faulty declaration and the correct repair.

fixes.label: Change the return type to async Task.
Keep async void and add a try/catch that swallows errors.

steps.explanation: async Task is awaitable and propagates exceptions. async void is only appropriate for top-level event handlers.
hints: async void hides completion and exceptions.
The caller cannot await an async void method.
Use async Task for ordinary asynchronous methods.
Change the declaration to private async Task LoadTotal().
